summary: This program figures out how many people can each get two slices of cake from a tray of 23 slices, and how many slices are left over. It demonstrates Java's integer division operator (/) and the modulus operator (%).

lines.text: Every Java program lives inside a class, and the class name must match the file name, so this code belongs in DessertServingsCalculation.java.
This is the method Java runs first when the program starts; all the work below happens inside it.
The total supply of cake slices is stored in an int variable, which holds whole numbers only.
Naming the serving size as a variable rather than typing 2 everywhere means one edit changes the whole calculation.

lines.code: int peopleFullyServed = slicesAvailable / slicesPerPerson; // integer division
lines.text: Dividing one int by another gives an int: 23 / 2 is 11, not 11.5, because Java throws away the fractional part rather than rounding. That is exactly what you want here, since a person served only half a portion is not fully served.
The % operator returns the remainder of the division, so 23 % 2 is 1 -- the single slice that could not complete another full serving.
The + operator joins text to a number here, converting the int into characters so it can be printed as part of the sentence.
Reporting the two computed results together shows how division and modulus split a quantity into complete groups plus a remainder.
